recentItems.title: Fascism built the AI bubble. Will an apocalypse burst it? | Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor | Deja Vu
recentItems.description:
Disaster capitalism once meant cashing in on a crisis. What happens when the crisis never ends? From Israel’s war in Gaza to AI and the far right, authors Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor trace the alliance linking tech billionaires, religious end-timers and ethnonationalists. They ask: who profits from the business of collapse? And what are the alternatives?

In this episode: 

- Naomi Klein, Author, End Times Fascism
- Astra Taylor, Author, End Times Fascism

Episode credits:

This episode was produced by Mohamed Hassan, Marcos Bartolomé and Sonia Bhagat. It was edited by Alexandra Locke. Our engagement producer is Adam Abou-Gad. Our sound designer is Alex Roldan.

recentItems.title: “This government is scared”: Can Modi survive India's youth uprising? | UpFront
recentItems.description:
A wave of youth-led protests is challenging Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government, fuelled by anger over leaked exams, dwindling economic opportunities and allegations of voter suppression. As authorities face accusations of mass arrests and an increasingly heavy-handed crackdown on dissent, is Modi's grip on power beginning to weaken? And could India's younger generation pose the biggest challenge yet to his rule?

This week on UpFront, Marc Lamont Hill speaks with Indian writer and journalist Aatish Taseer about the future of Indian democracy and whether the protests could mark a turning point for Modi's government.

recentItems.title: US-Iran tensions escalate: Tankers on fire in Strait of Hormuz
recentItems.description:
Tensions between the United States and Iran escalate as the IRGC claims drone strikes on a US military radar system in Bahrain, while two oil tankers catch fire in the Strait of Hormuz after reportedly hitting naval mines. Bahrain says the drones were intercepted.

Reporting from Tehran, Al Jazeera's Resul Serdar examines Iran's shift towards active deterrence, the diplomatic deadlock and warnings from Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf about the consequences of renewed conflict.

recentItems.title: Australia's gambling industry: the ads, the money, the lobby | The Listening Post
recentItems.description:
From slot machines to betting apps, gambling is a big part of Australian culture. Advertisers know it is something people often do with friends, and they have tapped into that trend. Australians are bombarded with slick marketing that promotes betting with mates.

Elettra Scrivo reports on one of the world's most entrenched gambling industries, the advertising that props it up and the lobby that protects it.

Featuring:
Alex Russell – Research Fellow, Experimental Gambling Research Lab
Kate Seselja – Founder, The Hope Project Australia and co-chair, Gambling Harm Lived Experience Experts
Steve Cannane – Reporter, ABC Australia Four Corners

recentItems.title: Brief: Israel attacks Nasser Hospital for 7th time, Iran claims strikes on US base | The Take
recentItems.description:
This week: 401 days after the declaration of a ceasefire in Gaza,  Israel has killed at least 1,643 Palestinians there. Iran claimed attacks on a US base in Bahrain. Israel bombed Nasser Hospital in central Gaza for a seventh time. Israeli pogroms continued in the occupied West Bank.

Israel has killed at least 74,695 Palestinians in Gaza since October 7, 2023.

In this episode:

- Mohamed Vall, Al Jazeera Correspondent  
- Tareq Abu Azzoum, Al Jazeera Correspondent
- Nour Odeh, Al Jazeera Correspondent
